Environmental data

Plotting environmental data

biodiversityDS .

Species distribution models require environmental data (e.g., raster layers with temperature gradients). Such data are available in digital format (e.g., online repositories like Bio-ORACLE). The first approach is to map the raster layers.

# load libraries
library(terra)
# make a vector with the desired file names
myFiles <- list.files("../Data/Raster data", pattern = "Present Benthic", full.names = TRUE)
# inspect the files
myFiles
## [1] "../Data/Raster data/Present Benthic DissolvedMolecularOxygen Mean.tif"   
## [2] "../Data/Raster data/Present Benthic OceanTemperature LtMax.tif"          
## [3] "../Data/Raster data/Present Benthic OceanTemperature LtMin.tif"          
## [4] "../Data/Raster data/Present Benthic pH Mean.tif"                         
## [5] "../Data/Raster data/Present Benthic Salinity Mean.tif"                   
## [6] "../Data/Raster data/Present Benthic SeaWaterVelocity LtMin.tif"          
## [7] "../Data/Raster data/Present Benthic TotalPrimaryProductionPhyto Mean.tif"
S4 // Downloading and managing environmental data in R

biodiversityDS .
# Open a raster layer with the global sea surface temperature
environmentData <- rast(myFiles)
# inspect the raster object
plot(environmentData)

Downloading environmental data in R

biodiversityDS .

Extracting environmental layers from data warehouses such as Bio-ORACLE.

From Bio-ORACLE

# load libraries
library(bDSSDMTools)
# list available layers in Bio-ORACLE
layersList <- list_multiple_layers()
# inspect the layers
head(layersList)
dataset_id title
tas_baseline_2000_2020_depthsurf Bio-Oracle AirTemperature [depthSurf] Baseline 2000-2020.
tas_ssp119_2020_2100_depthsurf Bio-Oracle AirTemperature [depthSurf] SSP119 2020-2100.
tas_ssp126_2020_2100_depthsurf Bio-Oracle AirTemperature [depthSurf] SSP126 2020-2100.
tas_ssp245_2020_2100_depthsurf Bio-Oracle AirTemperature [depthSurf] SSP245 2020-2100.
tas_ssp370_2020_2100_depthsurf Bio-Oracle AirTemperature [depthSurf] SSP370 2020-2100.
S4 // Downloading and managing environmental data in R

biodiversityDS .

Layers can be easly downloaded using download_multiple_layers. Main arguments of download_multiple_layers() function:

  • variables (list) variable name to consider (e.g., c(“thetao”, “chl”, “so”)), summary statistic derived from the variable (e.g., c(“mean”, “min”, “max”, “ltmax”)) and vertical realm (e.g., c(“depthsurf”, “depthmean”, “depthmax”)).
  • experiment (Character) climate scenarios (e.g., c(“baseline”, “ssp126”, “ssp585”)).
  • decade (Numeric) the start year of the specific decade (e.g., c(2020, 2050, 2090)).
  • latitude (Numeric vector, length 2) spatial extent c(min_latitude, max_latitude).
  • longitude (Numeric vector, length 2) spatial extent c(min_longitude, max_longitude).
  • exportRaster (Logical, Default: TRUE) If TRUE, the function will combine layers into a single multi-layer SpatRaster.
  • directory (Character string or NULL, Default: NULL) path to a directory. If provided, the function saves each layer as an individual .tif file within that directory.

Refer to the Session-P-S04-BO-Components.html documentation file for more details.

S4 // Downloading and managing environmental data in R

biodiversityDS .
# download layers
variables <- list(var1 = c("thetao", "ltmax", "depthsurf"), var2 = c("no3", "ltmin", "depthsurf"))
environmentalLayers <- download_multiple_layers(variables = variables, experiment = c("baseline"),
    decade = c(2010))
# plot layers
plot(environmentalLayers, axes = TRUE)

S4 // Downloading and managing environmental data in R

biodiversityDS .

Combining or comparing layers

# make list of variables
variables <- list(var1 = c("thetao", "ltmax", "depthsurf"))

# download present-day layer
temperaturePresent <- download_multiple_layers(variables = variables, experiment = c("baseline"),
    decade = c(2010), longitude = c(-15, 45), latitude = c(25, 50))

# download end-of-century layer
temperatureFuture <- download_multiple_layers(variables = variables, experiment = c("ssp370"),
    decade = c(2090), longitude = c(-15, 45), latitude = c(25, 50))

# determine the degree of temperature change (anomaly)
temperatureAnomaly <- temperatureFuture - temperaturePresent
S4 // Downloading and managing environmental data in R

biodiversityDS .
# plot layer
plot(temperatureAnomaly, main = "Sea surface temperature change (anomaly)", axes = TRUE)
